records.label: Two unrelated patients with 4q25 deletion

phenotypes.text: severe oligodontia of primary and permanent dentition

quotes: We report two unrelated patients with 4q25 de novo deletion encompassing LEF1, associated with severe oligodontia of primary and permanent dentition, hypotrichosis and hypohidrosis compatible with hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia.
Taurodontism and a particular alveolar bone defect were also observed in both patients.

records.label: Individuals with monoallelic LEF1 variants
quotes: Monoallelic variants in LEF1 were detected in 11 affected individuals from 4 unrelated families
The phenotypic spectrum includes various limb malformations, such as radial ray defects, polydactyly or split hand/foot, and ectodermal dysplasia.
records.genotype_reason: single heterozygous variant; mode as stated for the family

quotes: Hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia in a family: expanding spectrum of LEF1-related disorders.

notes.statement: Dufour et al. (2022) stated that, depending on the type and location of LEF1 variants, inheritance of this condition can be either autosomal dominant or autosomal recessive.
quotes: Depending on the type and location of LEF1 variants, the inheritance of this novel Mendelian condition can be either autosomal dominant or recessive.

notes.statement: Dufour et al. (2022) found that haploinsufficiency or loss of DNA binding by LEF1 was associated with a mild to moderate phenotype, whereas loss of beta-catenin binding caused by biallelic variants was associated with a severe phenotype.
quotes: Our functional data indicate that 2 molecular mechanisms are at play: haploinsufficiency or loss of DNA binding are responsible for a mild to moderate phenotype, whereas loss of β-catenin binding caused by biallelic variants is associated with a severe phenotype.

notes.statement: Using immunofluorescence, immunoblotting, pulldown assays, and RNA sequencing, Dufour et al. (2022) found that transcriptomic studies revealed an alteration of WNT signaling associated with LEF1 variants.
quotes: Cellular consequences were characterized by immunofluorescence, immunoblotting, pulldown assays, and/or RNA sequencing.
Transcriptomic studies reveal an alteration of WNT signaling.

notes.statement: Lévy et al. (2020) said their findings gave further evidence that LEF1 haploinsufficiency plays a role in ectodermal dysplasia. They noted that no pathogenic variants involving LEF1 had previously been reported in humans.
quotes: So far, no pathogenic variants or variations involving the LEF1 gene have been reported in human.
We provide further evidence for LEF1 haploinsufficiency role in ectodermal dysplasia and delineate its clinical phenotype.

notes.statement: Galceran et al. (2004) found that LEF1 bound multiple sites in the Dll1 promoter in vitro and in vivo. Mutating these LEF1-binding sites impaired expression of a Dll1-LacZ transgene in the presomitic mesoderm. Induced expression of LEF1-beta-catenin activated endogenous Dll1 in fibroblastic cells. The authors concluded that Wnt signaling can affect the Notch pathway through LEF1-mediated regulation of Dll1.
quotes: LEF1 was found to bind multiple sites in the Dll1 promoter in vitro and in vivo. Moreover, mutations of LEF1-binding sites in the Dll1 promoter impair expression of a Dll1-LacZ transgene in the presomitic mesoderm.

Finally, the induced expression of LEF1-beta-catenin activates the expression of endogenous Dll1 in fibroblastic cells. Thus, Wnt signaling can affect the Notch pathway by a LEF1-mediated regulation of Dll1.

notes.statement: Galceran et al. (2004) showed that in mice, a targeted mutation of Lef1 that abrogates LEF1 function and impairs the activity of coexpressed TCF factors affected somite patterning and the expression of Notch pathway components.
quotes: show that a targeted mutation of Lef1, which abrogates LEF1 function and impairs the activity of coexpressed TCF factors, affects the patterning of somites and the expression of components of the Notch pathway
